extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in race, media, comedy, and ethics (general public, media critics, comedians/writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and critique of how public figures (especially comedians) recount personal experiences of racism and marginalization, focusing on truthfulness, harm to individuals and communities, and workplace/fact-checking practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness in recounting racist experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid fabricating or wildly embellishing stories about being subjected to racism; falsehoods about racism are harmful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece argues that 'lying about racism does a huge disservice to racial and ethnic minorities' and that Minhaj’s fabrications make him 'the boy who cried racist wolf,' which can be used by denialists to dismiss real claims of racism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on 'emotional truths' to justify falsehoods
rubrics_metrics.description: Claiming that fabricated anecdotes reflect 'emotional truths' is not an adequate defense for presenting untrue events as fact in public work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author calls Minhaj's defense — that his lies reflect 'emotional truths' — 'intellectually dishonest' and says it alienates potential allies and undermines genuine experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent harm to named or identifiable individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid depicting private individuals in ways that expose them to harassment, doxxing, or sustained abuse without verified grounds or consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Minhaj projected images of a real woman (his alleged prom date) during performances, which led to years of harassment and doxing; creators should consider these downstream harms before including identifying details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize personal privilege and intersectionality
rubrics_metrics.description: A storyteller should acknowledge their own privileges and the complexity of identities rather than presenting a reductive victim/aggessor narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes Minhaj omits his privilege (e.g., being half-white, elite education, financial security) and thus erases intersectionality, framing himself uniformly as a victim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold rigorous fact-checking and respond to internal challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers and shows should have and honor rigorous fact-checking processes and not marginalize or silence staff who raise factual concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: According to the piece, two researchers tasked with fact-checking were removed from meetings and sidelined; Minhaj defended the show's fact-checking as 'extremely rigorous' despite these reports — a mismatch creators should avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not weaponize others' suffering for personal advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Creators should not co-opt or exploit other people's pain and marginalization to advance their own careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article argues Minhaj 'co-opted' the pain of people of color to advance his career, which in turn makes it harder for less-privileged people to be believed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider how narratives may embolden denialists or oppressive movements
rubrics_metrics.description: When crafting narratives about racism, creators must consider whether fabrications could be used by racism-denying actors to minimize systemic injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece cites research on 'racism denial' and warns that high-profile falsehoods provide fodder for political strategies that minimize racism and 'buttress white supremacy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid simplistic, binary portrayals of oppressor and victim
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid reductive storytelling that always casts white people as aggressors and people of color as perpetual victims without nuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author criticizes Minhaj for painting 'a reductive picture of racism' that disregards intersectionality and nuance, turning complex dynamics into a flat David-vs-Goliath trope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice accountability when falsehoods are exposed
rubrics_metrics.description: Public figures should acknowledge inaccuracies, take responsibility for harms caused by fabricated stories, and make reparations rather than defensively insisting on their right to embellish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes Minhaj at times admitted certain incidents 'never actually happened' yet defended them; it frames this defensive posture as inadequate and harmful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain ethical workplace behavior toward colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Those producing media should not tolerate or enable gender discrimination, retaliation, or the marginalization of staff who raise concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece references legal claims by women who worked on 'The Patriot Act' alleging discrimination and retaliation, and describes how sidelining fact-checkers contributes to unethical work environments.
